requirement:
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
rationale:
I judged the tests against each clause of `requirements.references.rust_item_selectors`. I found no gap. I did not request implementation source.

- **Syntactic-ancestry segments** (`fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, `mod[local]/fn[run]`):
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` and `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs` assert exact selectors for nested items.
  - These include `mod[local]/fn[run]`, `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`, `trait[Trait]/fn[read]`, and `extern[C]/fn[puts]`.
  - The first test also asserts that `resolve` round-trips each selector.
  - `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` in `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs` asserts the full selector list for a module with a documented and attributed function.

- **No cross-file module resolution:**
  - `functions_in_a_separate_module_file_are_selected_within_that_file` asserts that `mod local;` in `lib.rs` yields only `mod[local]`.
  - It asserts that `local.rs` yields exactly `fn[run]`, with no `mod[local]` prefix.
  - `mod[external]` is also asserted in the two selector tests.

- **Item kinds that MUST be outline nodes:**
  - Functions and methods are covered by `fn[...]` and `impl[Thing]/fn[run]`.
  - Structs, enums, unions, traits, impls, modules, macros (`macro[make]`), constants, statics, type aliases (`type[Alias]`, `trait[Trait]/type[Item]`), and extern blocks (`extern[C]`, `extern[Rust]`) are asserted in `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry`.
  - The check on `contents.outline().items` kinds in `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` also asserts `mod`, `fn`, and `struct`.

- **Impl naming:**
  - `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]` are asserted directly.
  - `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]` covers a non-path self type.
  - `impl[Wrapper<T>/Trait]` covers a generic self type, and `impl[Thing/core::fmt::Display]` covers a qualified trait path.

- **Anonymous nodes:**
  - `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` asserts that two `use` declarations get distinct `use@...` selectors.
  - `item_macros_are_anonymous_nodes_and_expression_macros_are_not` asserts `macro@<12 hex>` selectors for item-position macro invocations at top level, in an impl, and in a module.
  - The same test asserts that two macros are distinct and that macros in function bodies are not nodes.

- **Selector spelling documented:** `every_profile_mapping_is_documented` asserts that `md/reference.md` contains each documented Rust selector form, including `use@3f2a9c01b7de`. It also asserts the anonymous-use/macro sentence and the "Modules are never resolved across files" sentence.

All the tests carry `{test}` references to the subject.

text: :::{req} rust_item_selectors
The Rust outline profile under {cite}`requirements.references.outlines` MUST
identify items by segments describing their syntactic ancestry within the file,
such as `fn[run]`, `struct[Packet]`, and `mod[local]/fn[run]`, and MUST NOT
resolve Rust modules across files. Functions, methods, structs, enums, unions,
traits, impls, modules, macros, constants, statics, type aliases, and extern
blocks MUST be outline nodes. Impl segments MUST be named by their syntactic self
type and optional trait path, as `impl[Thing]` and `impl[Thing/Trait]`. `use`
declarations and other items without a suitable name MUST be anonymous. Selector
spelling MUST be documented.
:::{req} outlines
Habeas MUST parse Rust, Python, TypeScript, CSS, Markdown, TOML, and YAML
sources with pinned tree-sitter grammars, selected by file extension compared
case-insensitively. When validating outline evidence inputs, Habeas MUST report
the line of the first syntax error in a recovered outline. Every
other text file MUST use a plain-text profile in which each line that is not
blank is an anonymous outline node of kind `line`. Each supported language MUST
have an outline profile that maps grammar node kinds to short outline kind names
and, for each mapped kind, states whether a node is named, and by which fields
or children, or anonymous. Only mapped kinds MUST appear in the outline, except
that a Markdown profile MAY additionally recognize colon-fenced directive
containers under {cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fence_precedence`
and expose them as outline nodes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.sources.markdown.fenced_blocks`. Such containers MUST
preserve source ranges and containment, and MUST NOT be recognized within
literal code or raw HTML. Other nodes MUST be transparent, so their outline
descendants appear under the nearest outline ancestor. A profile MAY attach grammar siblings to an outline
node, such as Rust attributes and doc comments preceding an item, so the outline
tree need not match the grammar tree exactly; attached siblings are part of that
node for its line range and hash. Every file's outline MUST have a root node
for the whole file, independent of language. Source in no other outline node,
such as top-level statements no profile maps, MUST belong to the root node;
profiles MUST NOT invent fallback kinds for it. Comments MUST NOT be outline nodes. Profiles MUST be
documented. Upgrading a grammar or profile MAY change outlines and MUST be
treated as a deliberate change.
